stage_1.document_name: Notarially certified copy of the full passport (bio-data page and signature page) of each proposed director, secretary, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
stage_1.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the country of residence of the individual (authenticating the underlying passport issued by the national passport authority)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), as amended, ss 10–24 (incorporation, name, registered office), ss 30–33 (share capital and subscriber agreement), ss 34–37 (constitution and default rules), ss 46–49 (certificate of incorporation and legal personality), ss 91–96 (share registers and share certificates), ss 110–113 (share allotment), ss 122–123 (execution of documents), ss 128–139 (directors' duties and powers), ss 140–153 (appointment and disqualification of directors), ss 200–211 (annual returns and registers); s 151(2)–(3) (director residency requirement); Income Tax Act 2007 ss CW 20–CW 22 (non-resident company foreign-sourced income exemption, which operationalizes the client's 'Tax Exempt Zone' classification for an International Company conducting business wholly outside New Zealand); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 ss 31–36 (reporting entity obligations).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies — New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online Application for Registration of a Company (NZCO 1) filed electronically through the New Zealand Companies Office Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up share capital exists for a New Zealand company under the Companies Act 1993; shares may be of no par value and may remain partly or fully unpaid at incorporation. There is no escrow, bank guarantee, or capital deposit requirement. All allotments, distributions, and share buy-backs must satisfy the solvency test prescribed in s 4 of the Act, and, where shares are issued for non-cash consideration, a solvency certificate must be filed with the Registrar within 20 working days of the allotment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
IN THE MATTER of the Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand) and IN THE MATTER of [Company Name] Limited (the 'Company')

FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE INCORPORATOR AND FOUNDING DIRECTOR

RESOLVED, with the consent of the sole incorporator and founding director, by way of the first board resolution of the Company, as follows:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The allotment and issue of 100 fully-paid ordinary shares of no par value in the issued share capital of the Company to the founding subscriber(s) at a subscription price of NZ$1.00 per share, aggregating to NZ$100.00 subscribed capital, be and is hereby ratified, confirmed, and approved; and the secretary or any director is hereby authorized to enter such allotments in the share register, to issue share certificates, and to take all steps necessary to record the beneficial ownership held for the virtual concert metaverse platform.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [Registered Office Street Address, City, New Zealand], being a physical address in New Zealand at which documents may be served during ordinary business hours, and the person or entity occupying such office is hereby appointed the Company's agent for service of documents pursuant to s 31 of the Companies Act 1993.

3. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: [Director Full Name], holding nationality [Nationality] and passport number [Number], be and is hereby appointed as sole Director, Chairperson, and Chief Executive Officer of the Company; [Secretary Full Name] be and is hereby appointed as Company Secretary (where applicable); and [Compliance Officer Full Name] be and is hereby appointed as the AML/CFT Compliance Officer of the Company under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.

4. BANKING, PAYMENT, AND TREASURY MANDATES: The Chairperson is hereby authorized, acting alone, to open and operate corporate bank accounts with licensed New Zealand and international banks, to appoint payment facilitation providers including Stripe and licensed USDC custodians, to execute treasury and foreign-exchange mandates, and to execute all merchant agreements and digital-asset custody agreements necessary for the receipt of virtual ticket proceeds and settlement of artist royalties.

5. STATUTORY FILINGS AND OPERATIONS: The Chairperson is hereby authorized to register the Company with the Inland Revenue Department for income tax, GST, and employer obligations, to file all annual returns and notices with the Registrar of Companies, and to take all such incidental and lawful steps as may be required to carry on the business of virtual performance hosting and digital ticket tokenization in conformity with the Companies Act 1993 and the Company's constitution (if adopted).

RESOLVED FURTHER that the resolutions set out herein shall remain in full force and effect until revoked, varied, or superseded by a subsequent resolution duly adopted by the board of directors of the Company.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Tāke) of New Zealand — myIR secure online portal (https://www.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident International Company applying for a New Zealand IRD number must submit form IR596 (Non-resident Company IRD Number Application) accompanied by the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, registered office details, and declarations identifying directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners. Applications may be filed directly with the IRD or through a New Zealand tax agent; the IRD issues an IRD number without requiring physical local presence or registration of a New Zealand branch, provided the company's activities are confined to offshore-origin income streams.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand law does not provide a US-style check-the-box entity classification election. Eligible closely held companies may elect Look-Through Company (LTC) treatment under Subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, or transitional Qualifying Company (QC) election under Subpart HA. Hybrid mismatch rules in Subpart FH and controlled foreign company (CFC) attribution rules in Subpart FE require foreign hybrid entity notifications and CFC attributing interest elections to be lodged with the IRD where cross-border structures are involved.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 for domestic supplies of goods and services; for non-resident suppliers of remote/digital services under the offshore supplier registration regime, the same NZD 60,000 annual threshold applies based on taxable supplies to New Zealand consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government-validated e-invoicing. Voluntary Peppol-compliant e-invoicing is available through certified service providers. GST returns are lodged electronically through myIR on a two-monthly, six-monthly, or annual basis depending on turnover; no real-time tax clearance API is required for issuing invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 applies where goods are exported from New Zealand within 28 days of supply and are not subsequently re-imported, and where services are supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply with the services performed outside New Zealand. For virtual concert metaverse ticketing and digital token services, zero-rating is available if the supply is made to a non-resident recipient outside New Zealand and the benefit of the supply is received outside New Zealand; if the recipient is in New Zealand, the offshore supplier must charge GST at 15% under the remote services reverse-charge regime.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged via the New Zealand Customs Trade Single Window (TSW)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal of exported goods
Inward Remittance Certificate or settlement record from the acquiring bank/payment service provider evidencing FX repatriation and consideration receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Exporters claiming zero-rating are subject to IRD audit of the documentary trail, export timing, and foreign exchange repatriation. Under the Tax Administration Act 1994, an abusive tax shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the GST shortfall may apply for evasion or fraudulent zero-rating claims, alongside use-of-money interest and retrospective GST assessments clawing back previously refunded input credits. Knowingly false export claims may also attract fines and prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) — the central bank responsible for monetary stability, currency issuance, foreign reserve management, and operation of the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESSA). Foreign exchange administration is exercised under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 rather than through a standalone exchange-control authority. Non-resident investment screening in protected assets is administered by the Overseas Investment Office (OIO) within Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand (LINZ) under the Overseas Investment Act 2005.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely floated and fully convertible; neither the current account nor the capital account is subject to exchange-control licensing, surrender requirements, or differentiated convertibility regimes. Inbound equity, ticket revenue, and intercompany loans may be converted into NZD or any reserve currency without central-bank approval, and dividends, royalty, interest, and management-fee remittances face no FX hurdle. The only material repatriation constraints are fiscal: non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) at 30% on non-imputed dividends or 15% on fully imputed dividends (treaty-reduced where a DTA applies), the approved issuer levy (AIL) of 2% on qualifying interest, and royalty withholding at 15% default or 10% treaty rate; these are cleared at the bank via the Inland Revenue IR872 tax-residence certificate and a completed withholding declaration, after which proceeds are credited in freely usable currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory timeline, no minimum repatriation percentage, and no mandatory conversion ratio for export or export-of-services receipts; the former Exchange Control Regulations were revoked and no surrender obligation exists today. Digital-service exporters, including the CK International Company hosting virtual concerts and tokenising tickets, may retain export earnings offshore in any currency or stablecoin, provided that: (i) cross-border wire transfers above NZD 10,000 and physical currency movements above NZD 10,000 are declared or reported by the reporting bank to satisfy AML/CFT and balance-of-payments statistical obligations; (ii) international telegraphic transfers carry an accurate purpose-of-payment classification (e.g., 'Services - Entertainment Services', 'Digital Ticketing Revenue') to support RBNZ statistics; and (iii) the underlying commercial invoices and smart-contract records substantiate the export-of-services nature of the receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency Operational Account (NZD with linked USD/EUR sweep); Capital Escrow Account for the initial shareholder injection
Business Operational Account (NZD) with Foreign Currency Account (USD/EUR); Capital Escrow sub-account for equity allotment proceeds
Everyday Business Account plus Foreign Currency Account (USD/EUR); Treasury Online for FX forwards and deposits
CashHub multi-currency Operating Account; trade finance desk for Commercial LC and SWIFT payment services
Business Operations Account (NZD) with savings/escrow sweep; limited multi-currency capability

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH as a complementary FX-treasury aggregation channel, MEDIUM as a primary settlement venue. Offshore digital EMIs (Airwallex, Wise Business, Currencycloud) may lawfully operate through New Zealand FSP registration under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Disputes Resolution) Act 2008, but they are not licensed deposit takers under the Deposit Takers Act 2023 and the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989 regime, cannot accept client deposits, do not access RBNZ settlement finality directly, and must safeguard client funds in segregated trust accounts at an NZ or Australian licensed bank. Legal constraints: (i) EMIs are reporting entities under the AML/CFT Act 2009 with transaction-monitoring and sanctions-screening obligations; (ii) USDC flows cannot settle into the NZD banking system without conversion through a licensed virtual asset service provider (VASP); (iii) EMI balances are not covered by the statutory deposit compensation scheme (NZD 100,000 cap under the Deposit Takers Act 2023) which protects only licensed deposit taker customers. Recommended architecture: tier-1 NZ bank as the primary settlement vault, the EMI as a controlled FX/liquidity aggregation node for USD/EUR outbound flows, and a regulated VASP for stablecoin on/off-ramp, all connected through a single treasury management system.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No NZ statute mandates an in-branch physical interview for a non-resident International Company; remote onboarding is permitted under enhanced due diligence where the company maintains a NZ registered office and a NZ-resident director or agent for service of documents (section 31, Companies Act 1993). In practice, the major banks (ANZ, ASB, BNZ) require a live video-conference KYB session with the ultimate beneficial owner, the trustee of the offshore trust (where relevant), and the authorised signatories, supported by an apostilled power of attorney and notarised certified copies of the Certificate of Incorporation, constitutional documents, register of charges, beneficial-ownership register, and board resolutions. Westpac and Kiwibank frequently attach a face-to-face 'first-principal' meeting at their Auckland or Wellington corporate banking centre where annual treasury flows exceed NZD 2 million or the entity bears a Tax-Exempt Zone classification, to verify commercial substance and the USDC conversion policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate shareholder with Tax-Exempt Zone classification and zero NZ corporate tax liability triggers the bank's offshore-tax-transparency review and potential 'shell entity' suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: (i) Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of the CK International Company; (ii) binding tax-exemption ruling or confirmation from Inland Revenue; (iii) beneficial-ownership register filed with the NZ Registrar of Companies, plus a redacted trust deed identifying the trustee and statement of beneficiaries; (iv) economic-substance file comprising the metaverse-event service agreement (ISIC 7110 scope), NZ registered-office lease, contractor/employment arrangements, and a transfer-pricing policy; (v) source-of-funds declaration with 6-month projected ticket-revenue flows; (vi) board resolution authorising account opening and the signatory matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume consumer ticket receipts aggregated through Stripe and international card networks produce unexplained third-party origin of funds and cross-border volume spikes inconsistent with a new entity's profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: (i) executed Stripe merchant service agreement setting out settlement currency and payout schedule; (ii) transaction-flow diagram from ticket purchaser to Stripe to the NZ bank account; (iii) 90-day settlement statements with merchant IDs, payer geographies, and refund/chargeback history; (iv) PCI DSS attestation for the payment stack and the digital-ticket smart-contract address; (v) local ledger reconciliation of ticket revenue against ancillary merchandise and platform fees; (vi) event-organiser certificate confirming the virtual concert schedule and the ISIC 7110 business scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: USDC token receipt is categorised as higher-risk by NZ banks under the AML/CFT Act 2009, particularly where stablecoin originates from DEX or non-hosted wallets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: (i) issuer attestation from Circle (USDC) and a whitelist of approved smart contracts; (ii) AML/CFT onboarding certificate of the licensed VASP/on-ramp converting USDC to fiat, with proof-of-reserves; (iii) Chainalysis or Elliptic blockchain-analytics reports on the corporate wallet demonstrating no sanctioned or dark-market exposure; (iv) written treasury policy converting USDC to fiat within 24-48 hours with a non-custodial zero-balance wallet structure; (v) executed KYC declarations from all counterparty OTC desks and an undertaking to reject transfers from unhosted wallets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International Company with intangible IP and ticket-token branding but no audited financials or local physical assets fails the bank's economic-and-trade-sanctions substance screen.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier: (i) audited or reviewed financial statements of the CK IC for the latest financial year; (ii) registered NZ/APAC trademarks, domain registrations, and the metaverse-platform hosting agreement; (iii) full corporate tree from the CK IC to final beneficial owners with sanctions/PEP screening results; (iv) legal opinion from NZ counsel confirming Companies Act 1993 validity, beneficial-ownership registration, and non-applicability of OIO consent; (v) 12-month cash-flow projection evidencing the operational reality of the virtual-concert pipeline.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity via SWIFT MT103 from the parent/shareholder to the CK IC's NZD Capital Escrow Account, with remittance field 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION - SHARE SUBSCRIPTION' and purpose code 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital' for RBNZ balance-of-payments statistics. Pre-wire verification: (i) board/shareholder resolution approving the allotment; (ii) share register updated within 10 working days and a share-allotment filing lodged with the NZ Companies Office (section 76, Companies Act 1993); (iii) source-of-wealth file of the transferring entity; (iv) for the USDC component, conversion through an NZ-licensed VASP into NZD fiat before transmission, with the VASP settlement confirmation memo attached to the payment instruction; (v) no OIO consent is triggered because virtual-concert hosting and ticket tokenisation does not involve sensitive land or significant business assets (Overseas Investment Act 2005). To avoid NRWT/interest-withholding frictions, the injection must be true equity and not a shareholder loan; if a loan is used, the 2% AIL election must be made by the borrower. The receiving bank will match the purpose-of-payment tag to the executed event-platform agreement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements: (i) SWIFT MT103 wires for artist royalties, licensing, technology, and supplier payments from the NZD/USD operating account, referencing the dated commercial agreement and beneficiary identity; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 for merchandise or hardware procurement, issued by the tier-1 NZ bank's trade finance desk (applicant CK IC, beneficiary overseas supplier); (iii) domestic NZD payments settled via the RBNZ Exchange Settlement Account System (ESSA) and low-value items via the New Zealand Clearing Automated Payment System; (iv) USDC outbound settlements, where contractually agreed, executed only through the regulated VASP rail with fiat settlement to the beneficiary's bank or direct transfer to whitelisted contract addresses; (v) every outbound wire carries a valid purpose-of-payment code; prescribed international transactions above NZD 10,000 are reported to satisfy AML/CFT and statistical exchange-control obligations. Indicative pricing: MT103 NZD 15-45 per instruction; LC issuance 0.125%-0.25% per quarter per LC face value; no capital-control restrictions on frequency or size of disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/AUD) documented under an ISDA Master Agreement or bank master FX terms, with settlement referencing the WM/Reuters NZD fix
FX Swaps (spot-forward combinations) for short-dated NZD/USD liquidity repositioning without disturbing the cash position
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) to convert USD ticket receivables into NZD/EUR matching operating-cost bases
Vanilla FX Options (call/put/risk reversals) purchased or sold with premium-hedging limits for event-seasonality ticket revenue

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) on NZD or on Asian settlement currencies (CNH, KRW, INR) where a deliverable forward or onshore liquidity is legally or commercially unavailable, executed via an offshore NDF desk referencing the official NZD fixing
Collateralised arrangements under a Credit Support Annex (CSA) with the tier-1 bank for swap/forward exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return to the Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after the annual return date, which is the anniversary of the company's incorporation date or an alternative date approved by the Registrar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 45 per month or part thereof; continued failure to file for two consecutive annual periods triggers Registrar's notice of intention to remove the company from the New Zealand Register under the Companies Act 1993 deregistration provisions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the e-filed return is due by 7 July; for non-standard balance dates, the due date is the 7th day of the seventh month following the balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250, increased by a further NZD 250 if still outstanding 30 days later; late payment penalty of 1% per month and use-of-money interest accrue on any unpaid tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST Return (where the annual filing basis is elected)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For an annual GST period ending 31 March, the return is due on 28 May; other annual balance dates require filing by the last business day of the following month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 50 per return; late payment penalty of 1% per month and use-of-money interest apply to unpaid GST; continued non-compliance may trigger compulsory monthly filing and enforcement action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is compulsory for large for-profit entities under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, defined as having total assets exceeding NZD 60 million, annual revenue exceeding NZD 30 million, or 50 or more full-time employees in each of the last two consecutive accounting periods. FMC reporting entities and financial institutions regulated under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 are also required to file audited financial statements. Small and medium entities, including a typical virtual event hosting company, are exempt unless shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting rights request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP), principally New Zealand equivalents to International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS); non-large entities may apply the Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR) or other simplified Tier 3 reporting basis permitted under the Financial Reporting Act 2013.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual return filed with the Companies Office must confirm the current shareholding structure, the issued share capital, and the names and addresses of all registered members and directors. Every share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members within 10 working days of execution, and the resulting shareholding is reflected in the next annual confirmation. Any individual owning or controlling 25% or more of the company's shares or voting rights must be identified in the company's Beneficial Ownership Register, and the annual confirmation must verify the accuracy and currency of that register as at the confirmation date.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax-Exempt Zone International Company (CK_IC) deriving only foreign-source income is wholly exempt from New Zealand corporate income tax. Standard New Zealand resident corporate rate is 28%, applied only where the IC is managed and controlled in New Zealand or derives New Zealand-source income through a permanent establishment. No general statutory tax holidays exist for domestic New Zealand companies; a 15% R&D tax credit applies to eligible research and development expenditure for resident taxable entities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return filed electronically through Inland Revenue 'myIR' portal using the company IRD number and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). A tax-exempt International Company with no New Zealand-source income and no New Zealand permanent establishment has no IR4 filing obligation in New Zealand.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; New Zealand-resident companies also pay provisional tax in three instalments, commonly due 28 August, 15 January and 7 May.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Standard balance date of 31 March: IR4 return must be filed by 7 July following the income year. Non-standard balance dates follow the Inland Revenue balance-date schedule; terminal tax and due dates are aligned to the approved balance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income, including virtual concert ticket revenue, metaverse platform fees, NFT/token sale proceeds and USDC-denominated receipts converted to NZD.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident International Company with no New Zealand tax nexus, leave blank unless income is attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses, including event production, streaming rights, payment processor fees, metaverse infrastructure, royalty payments and operating costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses directly incurred in deriving New Zealand taxable income; global overhead allocations must be supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income or net loss after statutory adjustments, including disallowed capital expenditure and non-deductible entertainment costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no permanent establishment exists, report nil and attach a schedule demonstrating tax residence and source of income analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward and utilised against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only New Zealand-resident companies can utilise tax losses; a non-resident International Company cannot offset losses against income that is not assessable in New Zealand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable at the applicable corporate rate before credits and rebates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company is liable only for New Zealand-source income attributable to a permanent establishment or for NRWT on passive income streams.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty up to NZ$250 per return, late payment penalty of 1% of unpaid tax with additional monthly increments, use-of-money interest on outstanding balances, and shortfall penalties of 20% to 150% for unacceptable or fraudulent tax positions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: New Zealand statutory non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends is 30%; fully imputed dividends may qualify for a 15% NRWT rate. A Tax-Exempt Zone International Company distributing foreign-source exempt income to non-resident shareholders does not incur New Zealand dividend withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a double tax agreement reduction in New Zealand, the non-resident shareholder must provide the New Zealand payer with a valid foreign tax residency certificate and a completed Inland Revenue IR745 declaration before payment. The payer must retain the declaration and evidence for audit. Where treaty relief is claimed, the reduced rate is applied at source; otherwise NRWT is withheld at the statutory 30% dividend rate. For an offshore International Company distribution, no IR745 is required where the distribution has no New Zealand tax nexus.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: New Zealand domestic NRWT is 15% on royalties and 15% on interest; an approved issuer levy of 2% may apply to qualifying interest. Relevant double tax agreements may reduce royalty and interest withholding rates to 5%-15%, subject to the same TRC and IR745 protocol.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Cross-border connected-party transactions involving a New Zealand resident entity or permanent establishment require contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation where the aggregate transaction value exceeds NZD 10 million. Below that threshold, records sufficient to demonstrate arm's-length pricing must still be retained.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain a standalone domestic Economic Substance Regulations statute, but Inland Revenue applies the general anti-avoidance rule, controlled foreign company rules, permanent establishment principles and OECD guidance to challenge artificial structures. A CK_IC International Company claiming Tax-Exempt Zone treatment must satisfy applicable economic substance conditions, maintain real local presence, keep accurate records and ensure management and control are not exercised in New Zealand; failure to do so may result in re-characterisation, denial of exemption and NZ 28% tax assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting virtual concert ticket receipts, mischaracterising USDC proceeds as non-taxable, or filing a false IR4 or IC declaration that conceals New Zealand-source income earned through the International Company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the evaded tax under the Tax Administration Act 1994, plus use-of-money interest; criminal conviction may attract a fine of up to NZ$50,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns or cause suppression of income are jointly and severally liable for assessed shortfalls; travel bans, asset restraint orders and director disqualification may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abusive Use of Tax-Exempt Zone
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the CK_IC as an invoicing shell with no employees, premises, accounting records, or local management in the claimed jurisdiction, while concert production, ticketing and treasury decisions are managed from New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax-exempt status may be disregarded; New Zealand-source income is re-attributed to the managing entity and assessed at 28%, with shortfall penalties up to 150%, late payment interest and possible company strike-off for non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for assisting in a sham arrangement, restitution of diverted profits, director banning orders and criminal prosecution if the shell is used to defraud revenue authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing metaverse platform licence fees, streaming royalties or event production charges to an overseas related party at non-arm's-length amounts to shift New Zealand taxable profit into a zero-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may adjust the consideration, disallow excessive deductions, impose shortfall penalties of 20%-150% and charge use-of-money interest under transfer pricing rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve pricing without contemporaneous economic analysis may incur personal penalties for reckless or knowingly incorrect transfer pricing returns, including liability for the assessed shortfall.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting high-volume Stripe and USDC payments for virtual concert tokens without customer due diligence, source-of-funds verification or suspicious transaction reporting, in breach of the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties for body corporates may reach NZ$2 million per serious breach, with compliance orders, remediation directions and possible criminal liability for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers are subject to AML obligations; knowing involvement in laundering proceeds of crime may result in personal criminal prosecution, fines and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unreported Cryptocurrency and Digital Asset Proceeds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to include USD/USDC-denominated virtual ticket sales and secondary-market token gains in the IC's accounting records and tax filings, or converting ticket revenue into stablecoins to avoid bank scrutiny.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalty of 20% for an unacceptable tax position without reasonable care, escalating to 150% for evasion; unreported digital proceeds are assessed as income with interest accruing until paid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for civil penalties where the company cannot satisfy assessed tax, and for criminal fines or imprisonment if intentional non-disclosure of digital asset proceeds is proven.
